program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding passes; consolidate, admit, validate, and merge once after Wave 2000

source_provenance: Sider Scholar + NCBI PubMed exact-source verification
cumulative PMID collision index covering prior enrichment waves and current branch

policy.validation_strategy: PMID-level dedupe/source verification during authoring; expensive repository-wide validation only after Wave 2000

waves.focus: One-year RCT in 59 men age 55-80 found daily prunes did not improve total or lumbar-spine BMD beyond calcium/vitamin D control, although selected bone-turnover markers changed less than control.

GRADE-assessed meta-analysis of five RCTs and 401 postmenopausal women found potassium citrate reduced urinary NTX at one month but did not consistently improve CTX or P1NP at later time points; trial-sequential evidence remained insufficient for key formation markers.

Randomized crossover secondary analysis in 20 premenopausal women with obesity found Greek yogurt altered acute post-exercise bone-turnover markers versus an isoenergetic carbohydrate pudding; these short-term surrogate responses do not establish fracture or BMD benefit.

Triple-blind RCT in older men with type 2 diabetes found resistance training improved physical outcomes across groups, with protein and synbiotic-plus-protein arms showing selected metabolic, inflammatory and strength differences; combined interventions prevent strain- or protein-only attribution.

Systematic review of frail/pre-frail older adults found exercise consistently improved strength, gait and frailty status, while nutrition alone was modest/inconsistent and combined exercise-nutrition strategies generally outperformed nutrition-only approaches.

Randomized crossover study in eight trained men found four days of low carbohydrate availability under energy balance increased beta-CTX and lowered IGF-1 without changing P1NP or several endocrine markers; tiny acute physiology study does not establish long-term bone harm.

Randomized crossover study in 20 young adults found milk and Greek-yogurt conditions altered acute post-exercise bone-status markers compared with carbohydrate or water; biomarker responses are not evidence of long-term BMD or fracture prevention.

Twelve-week RCT in 72 healthy adults age 65 and older found a self-selected vegan diet reduced protein intake and skeletal-muscle measures versus habitual omnivorous eating, while a resistance-exercise vegan arm tested whether training could mitigate losses; diet quality/protein context is critical.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in 136 frail older adults found calcium-HMB added to the same exercise program produced greater improvement in SPPB physical-function scores and selected secondary measures than placebo.

Cluster RCT in 90 community-dwelling Vietnamese older adults with sarcopenia found exercise improved grip strength and gait speed versus education, while adding counseling plus a multinutrient supplement did not consistently outperform exercise alone on all outcomes.

Three-year DO-HEALTH secondary analysis in 1,848 older adults found vitamin D and omega-3 alone did not significantly change sclerostin, P1NP or beta-CTX, while home strength exercise reduced sclerostin; combination effects were marker-specific.

180-day placebo-controlled RCT in 80 adults with mild-to-moderate knee osteoarthritis found proprietary standardized Boswellia extract improved pain/function scores and selected MRI/cartilage biomarkers; efficacy remains formulation-specific.

Eight-week double-blind RCT in 31 adults with grade 2-3 knee osteoarthritis found a type I/II/III collagen product improved several pain, quality-of-life and selected functional outcomes versus placebo; very small sample and proprietary blend limit certainty.

Factorial RCT in older women with low muscle mass found HMB did not significantly add to resistance training for functional or compositional muscle quality; resistance training itself provided the clearer benefit.

14-week RCT in 40 active young men found specific collagen peptides plus resistance training increased Achilles tendon cross-sectional area and muscle thickness more than training alone, but tendon stiffness and strength gains did not differ between groups.

Umbrella review of 15 systematic reviews found HMB evidence inconsistent for lean mass and strength and no review established a clear positive physical-function effect across aging/clinical populations.

Twelve-week double-blind RCT in older adults with sarcopenia found HMB plus resistance exercise improved grip strength, gait speed, chair-stand performance and muscle quality more than exercise plus placebo; small sample limits precision.

Longer-term double-blind RCT in active middle-aged adults found collagen peptides improved selected pain, activities-of-daily-living and mental/physical health measures in dose- and subgroup-dependent ways; effects were not uniform across all participants.

Three-week double-blind trial in fit men found replacing part of whey protein with collagen peptides did not improve muscle-damage markers or recovery of muscular performance versus the same total protein from whey alone.

Twelve-week double-blind trial in post-acute older adults with sarcopenia found calcium-HMB added to resistance rehabilitation improved selected SPPB domains and female grip strength, with some gains persisting at one year; findings are rehabilitation-context specific.

Five-arm RCT in 100 adults with knee osteoarthritis found proprietary Type-J bovine collagen peptides improved WOMAC, quality-of-life and selected imaging/biomarker outcomes, but product-specific dose comparisons should not be generalized to all collagen.

Cluster RCT in 72 institutionalized older adults found multicomponent exercise improved cognition, SPPB and muscle power, whereas HMB alone did not; adding HMB did not clearly outperform exercise for most endpoints.
Meta-analysis of six sarcopenia RCTs found HMB/HMB-rich supplements modestly improved grip strength but not gait speed, fat-free mass, skeletal-muscle index or several body-composition outcomes.

One-week double-blind resistance-training study in 25 young men found collagen peptides raised collagen-derived amino acids but did not further increase muscle connective or myofibrillar protein-synthesis rates versus placebo.

Meta-analysis of five RCTs and 257 older adults with sarcopenia found exercise plus HMB improved gait speed versus exercise plus placebo but did not significantly improve skeletal-muscle index; benefits were outcome-specific.
